fields.mechanism: Resonance absorption between photon energy and the potential barrier of a nanometer-scale dopant-rich region, which absorbs visible light photons without passing loss or thermal loss.
fields.intervention: Fabricate nanometer-scale n-type dopant-rich regions within the p-type silicon crystal of the solar cell to create localized potential barriers tuned to resonate with visible light photon energies, replacing conventional band gap absorption with this resonance mechanism.
fields.expected_effect: Elimination of passing loss and thermal loss for visible light frequencies, yielding a theoretical power conversion efficiency exceeding 70%.
fields.falsification_test: Measure the external quantum efficiency spectrum of the fabricated cell across visible wavelengths; if the device exhibits standard band-edge cutoff behavior or measurable sub-bandgap transmission instead of broadband visible absorption, the resonance absorption mechanism is not active.
fields.mechanism_source_span: By resonance absorption between photon energy and potential barrier of the Region, the cell can absorb most photons for visible light frequency without passing loss or thermal loss.

span_derivation.basis: shared content terms between span and mechanism+intervention; ratio < 0.20 = SPAN_UNDERIVED (the quoted span does not contain the mechanism's vocabulary)

fields.mechanism: Resonance absorption between photon energy and potential barrier of nm-scale n-type dopant-rich regions in p-type Si crystal, replacing conventional band gap absorption to eliminate passing loss and thermal loss.
fields.intervention: Remove the active carrier-collection drive across a bulk bandgap junction and instead structure the solar cell as a passive array of nm-scale n-type dopant-rich regions embedded in p-type Si, where the fixed structural potential barriers are dimensioned so their resonance energies match visible light frequencies, allowing photons to be absorbed directly by the barrier geometry without requiring active interband electronic transitions.
fields.expected_effect: Elimination of sub-bandgap transmission loss and above-bandgap thermalization loss, achieving theoretical power conversion efficiency exceeding 70%.

fields.mechanism: Resonance absorption between photon energy and potential barrier of nm-scale n-type dopant-rich regions in p-type Si crystal, combined with thermoelectric conversion of residual thermal gradients to recover non-radiative losses.
fields.intervention: Fabricate nm-scale n-type dopant-rich regions within the p-type silicon absorber layer of the solar cell, tuning the region dimensions so that their electrostatic potential barriers resonate with visible light photon energies; integrate a thermoelectric generator layer at the rear contact to convert any remaining thermalized carrier energy into additional electrical power via the Seebeck effect.
fields.expected_effect: Elimination of sub-bandgap transmission loss and above-bandgap thermalization loss through resonance absorption, while the thermoelectric layer recovers residual heat, yielding theoretical power conversion efficiency exceeding 70%.
fields.falsification_test: Measure external quantum efficiency across 400-700 nm wavelengths on a fabricated cell containing nm-scale n-type dopant-rich regions versus an identical cell without them; if the doped-region cell does not show near-unity absorption without corresponding thermal emission increase, and total measured efficiency does not exceed the Shockley-Queisser limit, the mechanism fails.
